C++, Python, ESP32 · Team Lead

\n

Scorpion-Lift BattleBot

\n

\n I built ESP32 firmware for Wi-Fi web-based robot control, including\n PWM output for two DC motors and three servo actuators. The system\n includes a heartbeat failsafe that stops the drive outputs within 580\n ms of signal loss and INA219 telemetry for current and voltage\n monitoring. The robot reached a 0.706 m/s drive speed, lifted 2 lb in\n 0.76 seconds, and ran continuously for two minutes.\n

\n View lab report ↗\n
\n \n\n \n
\n \n ×\n \n

C, ESP32, Embedded Systems · Team Leader

\n

Self-Balancing Biped

\n

\n I designed and programmed a two-legged self-balancing robot using an\n ESP32 and real-time feedback control loops. I applied control systems\n and embedded programming concepts to achieve dynamic stability and\n developed the firmware in C using Git-based version control. The\n project provided hands-on experience with hardware-software co-design,\n timing analysis, and system-level validation.\n

\n View project ↗\n
\n \n\n \n
\n \n ×\n \n

SystemVerilog, VHDL · Team Leader

\n

FPGA Apple ][ Reconstruction

\n

\n I reconstructed the legacy Apple ][ architecture on an Intel DE10-Lite\n FPGA by translating system-level specifications into RTL hardware. I\n migrated the memory subsystem from off-chip SRAM to on-chip block RAM\n to improve latency and synchronization. The project included FPGA\n design flow, synthesis, and timing analysis.\n
